newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CEO departure rumours not true - Australia's Optus.
newsitem.headline: CEO departure rumours not true - Australia's Optus.

text.p: Telephone carrier Optus Communications Pty Ltd said on Wednesday a newspaper report that Optus' chief executive officer Ziggy Switkowski was due to leave the company soon was not true.
"That is all it is - gossip. I don't know where they got that from. It is totally not true," said an Optus spokeswoman.
The Sydney Morning Herald reported in its CBD column that "the market was abuzz yesterday (Tuesday) with talk that Switkowski was all set to leave Optus."
The paper also said that there could be another delay to the proposed float.
Optus along with its major competitor Telstra Corp AOT.AX have both previously said they plan to float in 1997.
The Australian government plans to sell a third of its 100 percent stake in Telstra via a public float by the year end.

Analysts and media reports have speculated that it would be better for Optus, which is expected to raise up to A$1.5 billion, to float before Telstra, which is expected to raise a minimum of A$8 billion for government coffers.
"We are not dictated by the Telstra float. We plan to float as soon as possible and we hope it will be this year," said the Optus spokeswoman.
Optus originally planned to float last year, but was delayed due to litigation over its pay television arm Optus Vision and its former shareholders.
Optus Communications took full control of Optus Vision earlier this year, which ended the litigation.
The Sydney Morning Herald also reported on Wednesday that the merger of Optus Communications and Optus Vision was also slowing down the float process.

Optus's major shareholder Mayne Nickless Ltd has said it is keen to see the Optus float as soon as possible to realise funds that it could then invest in its core businesses of health care and transport.
At 3.50 p.m. (0550 GMT), Mayne shares were 17 cents down or 2.35 percent down at A$7.47 with nearly 1.4 million shares traded.
